title: An Alert the Night Learned to Ignore
story: The building sensor sent an alert whenever the cleaners ran hot water, so the night manager learned to swipe the message away. The system was not broken. Its threshold had been set for an empty pipe, and ordinary use now crossed that line. When a real drip started behind a cupboard, the same alert appeared and was dismissed with the others. By morning the plaster had softened. A technician raised the threshold, added a second warning if the alert lasted, and required a named person to close it. An alarm that cannot separate routine from harm trains people to ignore both.
